title: Kawat Ikat Getas Dipilin Putus, Kawat Licin Diamond Tetap Ulet
hook: Kawat ikat murah getas jadi putus saat dipilin tang waktu anyam besi cor
story: Di area tulangan kolom, pekerja sudah memelintir kawat pada persilangan besi dengan tang; roll Kawat Licin Diamond berlabel berdiri di keranjang di kiri bawah frame. Ia mengencangkan ikatan, lalu menekuk sisa kawat bolak-balik dua kali dan kawat tetap utuh. Ia mengusap permukaan kawat dengan sarung tangan, tidak ada serbuk karat, lalu menunjuk roll Diamond dan meminta penonton menyimpan video sebelum belanja besi cor.
caption:
Kawat ikat murah yang getas sering putus waktu dipilin tang, ikatan besi cor jadi harus diulang. Kawat Licin Diamond dari PT Intan Suar Kartika ulet dan tidak gampang karat, spek lengkapnya tanya lewat DM.
#kawatlicindiamond #kawatikat #besicor #materialbangunan

shots.prompt: Photorealistic live-action video, vertical 9:16, 12 seconds, one continuous take, shot on smartphone vlog camera held at chest height with gentle natural handheld sway and a slight three-quarter angle toward the rebar cage, real daylight documentary look, natural clean daylight neutral white balance, true-to-life colors, realistic matte human skin with visible fine pores, no plastic shine, no waxy skin, no glass skin, no yellow or orange tint, no artificial golden glow, zero CGI, authentic non-AI documentary look, clean frame without camera HUD, no REC icon, no viewfinder brackets, no camera display overlay, no on-screen text or captions of any kind. Location: a house construction site in North Sumatra, a column rebar cage of two vertical deformed steel bars with one square stirrup, grey cement dust on the ground, a blurred stack of rebar behind, bright overcast midday light from the open sky. On the ground at the lower-left of the frame, one upright sealed roll of the smooth galvanised wire from the single attached official reference photo stands inside a black plastic crate, its tight shiny silver coil and printed label facing the camera. An Indonesian male construction worker about 38 years old in a faded dusty blue long-sleeve work shirt, dark work trousers, grey cotton work gloves and a brown field cap stands at the cage; his face, gloved hands and torso stay in frame the whole take. PROP CONTINUITY RULE: from 0.0s to 12.0s exactly one labelled wire roll in the crate, one pair of pliers in his right hand, one short tied wire loop on the stirrup crossing and the two vertical bars are already visible and remain visible; no hammer, machete, bucket, wheelbarrow, vehicle, animal, extra person, extra wire roll or extra tool may appear, move in, fall or disappear at any instant, the wire thickness and the coil shape must not change, and no tie may come loose. BEATS: at 0.0s he already grips the pliers and twists the wire loop tight around the stirrup crossing in one firm unhurried motion and says in calm Indonesian with accurate lip sync, "Kawat ikat getas dipilin putus". From 4.0s he releases the pliers, takes the loose wire tail in both gloved hands and bends it ninety degrees back and forth twice; the wire stays bright silver and does not snap or flake, and he pauses about one second in silence. From 6.5s he runs his gloved thumb along the wire surface and turns it toward the lens, the galvanised skin stays clean with no white rust powder, while he says calmly, "Kawat Licin Diamond PT Intan Suar Kartika ulet anti karat". From 10.2s he looks at the camera, taps the labelled roll in the crate with his gloved knuckle and says, "Simpan dulu", then holds a small nod until 12.0s. Calm authoritative mandor tempo, roughly one and a half words per second, natural breathing pauses between the three spoken beats, real construction-site ambience with faint clink of steel and distant site noise, no music. Keep his face, clothing, gloves, cap, rebar cage and background consistent throughout every frame.
